objective: Determine whether rejections_by_tier / rejections_by_provider correctly exclude the three retry events or under-report them, and make the report reconcile its total against the retry count so an empty counter cannot read as no problem.
evidence: run readout 2026-09-22 — three retry events in stderr, both rejection counters empty
AGENTS.md convention 26 — an instrument's report states what it measured and nothing more; a reading mistakable for a stronger claim is a defect in the instrument
AGENTS.md convention 28 — an instrument asserts it computed its subject before it asserts anything about it
AGENTS.md convention 22 — an instrument's test simulates the condition it watches, end to end
ARCH-20260922-024 — the serving ledger made to report every tier; the same class
constraints: Read the three retry reasons from the committed stderr FIRST and quote each verbatim with its code path. Do not infer a cause you have not read.
Compare the guard condition on the retry path against the guard condition on the counter-increment path. State whether the counters' domain includes or excludes each retry reason.
If the counters are correctly narrow: do NOT widen them. Fix the report instead — a reconciliation stating attributed and unattributed retries, naming the excluded classes.
If the counters' domain includes a retry reason and it did not increment: that is under-reporting by three; fix the increment and state how many were missed.
Convention 28 applies: assert the retry total before asserting the breakdown. An unattributed count must never be silently zero.
One test per path, each simulating its condition end to end — an empty reply and a parse failure specifically (convention 22).
Open B23 in HANDOVER.md §4.2 with the finding, its severity and its evidence.
Do not conflate unrelated retry classes into one counter to make the numbers add up.
acceptance_criteria: The three retry reasons are quoted verbatim, each with its code path.
A ruling is stated: correct-and-narrow, or under-reporting, with the guard comparison as evidence.
The report reconciles: retry events equal attributed plus unattributed, and unattributed is printed.
A test simulates an empty reply and a parse failure end to end and asserts the count is not silently zero.
Suite count reported before and after.

verification.expected: One test per retry class passes.

rollback: Revert the commit; the counters return to their previous increments.
assumptions: The three retries were logged to a committed stderr. If the stderr is not committed, say so — the cause is then unobserved and the ruling must wait.
questions: Are the counters consumed by any report or dashboard that would now read 'zero rejections' beside a retry count? If so, name it — that surface is where the convention-26 defect lands.

preconditions.expected: Locate the increment sites; record each.
Locate the run's stderr by name. If absent, say so and treat the cause as unobserved.
